title: Yash and Kiara Just Dropped the Hottest Music Video of the Year. Nobody Was Ready.
excerpt: The 'Tabaahi' video from Toxic is four minutes of raw chemistry between two of Indian cinema's biggest stars — and it confirms Yash's gangster epic is the one to watch this August.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Kiara Advani's Instagram post sparked massive anticipation for the 'Tabaahi' music video.
  • The 'Tabaahi' video showcases intense chemistry between Yash and Kiara Advani.
  • Directed by Geetu Mohandas, 'Toxic' features a star-studded cast including Nayanthara and Huma Qureshi.
  • The film 'Toxic' will release globally on August 26, 2026, in multiple languages.
  • The music video is a teaser for the romantic ballad from Yash's upcoming gangster saga.

Kiara Advani posted a single word on her Instagram Story yesterday: *Tabaahi*. Below it, a time stamp — 8 July, 11:33 AM. That was all it took. The internet went into meltdown, and this morning, the music video delivered on every ounce of that hype.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=2cFnzFw7TE8

The official video for Tabaahi, the breakout romantic ballad from Yash's upcoming gangster saga Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups, is here. And it is devastating.

Sung by Vishal Mishra, who has quietly become the most reliable hitmaker in Hindi music, the track first dropped as an audio single on March 2 and immediately colonised every streaming playlist in the country. The composition is a romantic rock ballad that sounds like yearning distilled into melody — aching, urgent, impossible to skip. But the audio was only half the story. The video completes it.

Forbidden Love, Shot Like a Fever Dream

> "Tabaahi." — Kiara Advani**, on Instagram Stories

The Toxic Universe Keeps Expanding

Toxic has been building anticipation like a slow-burning fuse."**

The makers teased it with a question posted on the official Toxic page: *"What do you call a forbidden love that only exists in stolen time?"* Kiara answered with the song title, and the subtext was clear. In the film, she plays Nadia — a character the first look suggested carries both elegance and danger in equal measure — opposite Yash's Raya, a ruthless underworld figure navigating blood and betrayal across 1940s-70s Goa.

The music video leans all the way into that combustibility. There's smoke and candlelight and the kind of chemistry that makes you forget you're watching two people who met on a film set. Early reactions on social media are unanimous: this pairing works. It more than works — it smoulders.

![Fairy Tale — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Carl_Larsson_-_Little_Red_Riding_Hood_1881.jpg/3840px-Carl_Larsson_-_Little_Red_Riding_Hood_1881.jpg)

> "What do you call a forbidden love that only exists in stolen time? Tabaahi." — Kiara Advani, on Instagram Stories

The Toxic Universe Keeps Expanding

Star-Studded Cast of Toxic
›Yash plays Raya, a ruthless underworld figure.
›Kiara Advani portrays Nadia, a character of elegance and danger.
›Nayanthara plays Ganga, Raya's sister.
›Huma Qureshi is the primary antagonist, Elizabeth.
›Tara Sutaria and Rukmini Vasanth complete the formidable female ensemble.

Toxic has been building anticipation like a slow-burning fuse. Directed by National Award-winner Geetu Mohandas and co-written by Yash himself, the film is a period gangster drama set against the sun-bleached underworld of Goa. The cast is stacked: Nayanthara as Ganga, reportedly playing the protagonist's sister; Huma Qureshi as the primary antagonist Elizabeth; Tara Sutaria and Rukmini Vasanth rounding out what might be the most formidable ensemble of female talent assembled in an Indian action film.

The technical pedigree matches the star power. Cinematography by Rajeev Ravi. Score by Ravi Basrur, the man who gave KGF its thunderous sonic identity. Action choreography by Hollywood veteran JJ Perry alongside Indian duo Anbariv. The film was shot simultaneously in Kannada and English — a first for Yash — and will release in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, and Malayalam.

Originally slated for March 19, the release has been pushed to August 26, 2026, which puts it in a fascinating position — away from the crowded summer corridor and into a window where it could dominate screens across India.

Where to Watch for the Diaspora

Toxic is being positioned as a global release. Given Yash's massive international following from the KGF franchise — and the deliberate decision to shoot in English as well as Kannada — expect wide distribution in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and the Middle East. Subtitled and dubbed versions across five languages mean this isn't just a Sandalwood release; it's a pan-India, pan-world event.

Toxic's Global Release Strategy
›Scheduled release on August 26, 2026.
›Shot in Kannada and English, a first for Yash.
›Will be available in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, and Malayalam.
›Targeting audiences in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and the Middle East.
›Subtitled and dubbed versions to enhance accessibility.

The Tabaahi video is now streaming on YouTube. If the full film carries even half the heat of this four-minute tease, August can't come soon enough.

Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups releases in theatres worldwide on August 26, 2026.
